exact_statement: For disjoint uniform physical Boolean blocks F=g(f_1,...,f_k), let a_i=E(D_i g)^2 and gamma_ij be the probability, over other induced outputs, that the i,j gate face has corner product -1. With Q(f)=2^(1-n)N_odd(f), Q(F)=sum_i a_i Q(f_i)+(1/2)sum_{i<j}gamma_ij I(f_i)I(f_j). A query x in child h of F=A+B h has q_x(F)=t q_x(h)+(Inf_x(h)/2)I(1-2B^2), t=E B^2. For the explicit five-bit bent/point-flip selector c of DERIVATION.md, d=1/16,m=3/16,I(c)=37/16 and B_s(c)-Lbin(m,d)>1/4; hence its queried selector remains K=4 bad in every nontrivial disjoint outer composition. For F_LN=1-(1+P_N)(1-product_{j=1}^L c_j)/2, L,N>=1, I=[37L/16+(1-(3/16)^L)N]/2. A complete selectors-first tree spends at least L(4+N)/32 bad odd-face credit; for N=L^2 its ratio to I is at least L/53. A complete parity-first tree spends exactly L/8, ratio at most 4/37. The selectors-first signed mean residual bank is between zero and L(2L+4)16^(-(L+1)); it contains beta^2 log(1/M^2)/2+O(beta^2) at beta=-M/3. Thus at fixed K=4 every-tree O(I) credit is false, while this family satisfies a some-tree bound and has H/I tending to zero when N=L^2. No universal some-tree bound is asserted.
